compare_against: section 2.3, 'Equivalent rigid anchor plate (CBFEM)' column — NOT the 'CBFEM anchor plate design' column.
status: Cases C, D and E all run. All three DISAGREE. The unified 'flange lever arm' explanation proposed after C and D is REJECTED by E. See candidate_defect_9.

model.provenance: recovered 2026-08-30 by inverting the predictions, then CONFIRMED against the PROFIS report: plate 450x450x50, tension resultant at y = 175.0 mm (section 1.2), f'c 30 MPa, h 800 mm, hef 450, 2x2 @ 350, ca 450 all round (ANc 1,125,000 / ANco 810,000).
model.note_on_plate_grade: the module runs were made with S355JR; PROFIS's plate is A36. Grade affects the THICKNESS check only, not T_anchor, so the Case C comparison is unaffected. Re-run the thickness side with A36 before using it.

sign_convention: PROFIS takes N positive in TENSION. This module takes Pu positive in COMPRESSION. The module_input column below is already negated relative to the PROFIS sheet.

C.status: DISAGREES — module is 21.3% LOW, i.e. UNCONSERVATIVE

diagnosis.not_an_arithmetic_error: the module satisfies both equilibrium equations exactly: C - T = 150.000 kN against Pu = 150, and T*f + C*a = 120.000 kNm against Mu = 120. It also reproduces DG 1 Sect. 3.4 exactly: q_max*Y*(f + N/2 - Y/2) = 146,244 vs Pu*(e+f) = 146,250 kN.mm.
diagnosis.conclusion: PROFIS delivers the compression through the COLUMN FLANGE. Placing C at (d - tf)/2 = 144.65 mm and re-solving gives T = 307.532 kN against PROFIS's 306.481 — agreement to 0.34%. The module, following DG 1, spreads bearing into a rectangular block at the PLATE EDGE, which is a 54 mm longer lever arm and therefore less anchor tension.
diagnosis.equivalent_statement: the same gap is reproduced by running the DG 1 quadratic with an effective bearing width of 173 mm instead of the full 450 mm plate — i.e. roughly the IPE 300 flange (150 mm) plus spread.

severity.direction: unconservative in every combination tested — the module never reads high
severity.trend: the gap closes as the plate shrinks toward the profile: N=B=400 gives -10.1%, 420 gives -15.0%, 450 gives -21.5%. Consistent with the overhang being the mechanism.

caveats_on_this_run.profile_is_grossly_overloaded: section 3 reports Profile utilisation 342% NOT OK, and section 2.4.1 reports plastic strain 382.85% against a 5.00% limit. The CBFEM solution is therefore deep into gross plasticity, and the anchor force extraction — including the equivalent-rigid column — may be contaminated by that redistribution. RE-RUN Case C with a profile that is not failing before treating 306.481 as settled.
caveats_on_this_run.profis_flagged_the_plate: section 2.7: 'your specified anchor plate may not behave rigid'. Section 2.3: 'User accepted to consider the selected anchor plate as rigid by his/her engineering judgement.' PROFIS did not itself classify this plate as rigid.
caveats_on_this_run.anchors_also_fail: 142% on anchors, breakout 118% 'not recommended'. Does not affect the tension extraction, but the model as run is not a design.

C.flag_decision: DO NOT flip baseplate.eccentricity. Case C did not verify — it found a systematic unconservative bias. Logged as candidate defect #9.

D.branch: net uplift — NOT the DG 1 quadratic
D.status: was +23.7% (conservative) with the broken uplift branch; after the defect #9b fix the module gives 287.546 and reads -6.0%, i.e. UNCONSERVATIVE like C and E
D.expect: a disagreement, predicted in advance and for a DIFFERENT reason than Case C. The branch takes T = |Pu| + Mu/(2f), which implies sum(M) = Mu + Pu*f — an excess of exactly Pu*f = 26.25 kNm. Rigid-plate equilibrium with the plate-edge block gives T = 287.55 kN.
D.correction_to_earlier_prediction: the flange_model_prediction recorded here before the run was 262.20 kN. That was WRONG — an arithmetic slip: Pu was taken compression-positive (+150) in a case where the axial load is uplift (-150). Re-derived correctly the flange model gives 318.153 kN. The pre-run decision tree was built on the bad number and none of its three branches matched the actual 306.032; with the corrected prediction, the flange model is the closest of the three at +3.96%.

caveats_on_this_run.profile_overloaded: plastic strain 195.05% against a 5.00% limit (better than Case C's 382.85%, still far over). Re-run with a profile that is not failing.
caveats_on_this_run.profis_flagged_the_plate: section 2.7: 'your specified anchor plate may not behave rigid'. The rigid classification was accepted by the user, not by PROFIS.

D.flag_decision: DO NOT flip baseplate.eccentricity. Both branches it covers now have a measured disagreement.

defect_9b_fixed.was: T = |Pu| + Mu/(2f) — satisfied SigmaF but not SigmaM, residual |Pu|*f
defect_9b_fixed.now: the same DG 1 Sect. 3.4 quadratic the large-e branch uses, with Pu carried through signed: Y^2 - 2(f+N/2)Y + 2(Mu + Pu*f)/q_max = 0, T = q_max*Y - Pu. Writing it in (Mu + Pu*f) rather than Pu*(e+f) removes the singularity at Pu -> 0 that forced the split, since e = Mu/Pu is meaningless under uplift.
defect_9b_fixed.boundary: when Mu*1000 <= |Pu|*f no bearing zone closes, every anchor stays in tension and T = |Pu|. Continuous at the transition (Mu = 26.25 kNm for Pu = -150, f = 175).
defect_9b_fixed.consequence_stated_plainly: the fix makes Case D SMALLER and therefore LESS conservative: 378.571 -> 287.546, moving it from +23.7% above PROFIS to -6.0% below. Fixing an equilibrium error was still correct — the old number was conservative by accident, not by design, and it would have gone the other way on other geometries. But the uplift case governs a PEB base under wind, so this is a real reduction in a load case that matters and should be accepted knowingly.
defect_9b_fixed.what_it_does_not_fix: defect #9a — the bearing width and lever arm question. After this fix ALL THREE cases read low against PROFIS (C -21.3%, D -6.0%, E -38.9%), one consistent direction, one remaining cause. That is the point of unifying the branches: when the bearing model is decided, one change fixes every case.

E.purpose: registered before the run as the most discriminating case available, and as the test of whether PROFIS's near-equal 306.481 / 306.032 for C and D was coincidence.

predictions_registered_before_the_run.saturation_check: a third ~306 would mean something is saturating

E.status: DISAGREES — module is 38.9% LOW, i.e. UNCONSERVATIVE

outcome.saturation_ruled_out: PROFIS returned 275.997, not a third ~306. The C/D near-equality was coincidence; nothing is saturating.
outcome.flange_model_REJECTED: predicted 243.0 against an actual 275.997 = -12.0%. Having fitted C to +0.3% and D to +4.0%, it fails its first out-of-sample case. It was an over-fit to two points and is withdrawn as the explanation.
outcome.module_finding_STRENGTHENED: the large-e branch is unconservative in both compression cases and the gap WIDENS with axial load: -21.3% at Pu 150, -38.9% at Pu 500.

caveats_on_this_run.profile_worst_yet: plastic strain 538.17% against a 5.00% limit; equivalent stress 1394.30 MPa against fy 317.16. The run that killed the flange model is also the most grossly yielded of the three.

E_HEB300.purpose: control run — identical to Case E in every respect except the profile, changed IPE 300 -> HEB 300 (same depth 300, tf 10.7 -> 19, tw 7.1 -> 11, bf 150 -> 300, ~3x section modulus). Registered beforehand as the test of whether the 382-538% plastic strain in the earlier runs was contaminating the equivalent-rigid extraction.
E_HEB300.status: DISAGREES — module 38.9% LOW. Identical to the IPE 300 run.

outcome.plasticity_caveat_ELIMINATED: rigid column 276.0 against 275.997 with the yielded IPE 300 — identical to three figures. The equivalent-rigid extraction is insensitive to the profile, which is what it claims to be. And this was tested on the WORST-strained of the three runs (538.17%), so the same conclusion carries to C (382.85%) and D (195.05%).
outcome.coherence_check_passed: the CBFEM column DID move, 168.230/167.985 -> 147.4/148.5, while the rigid column did not. Exactly the right behaviour: CBFEM sees the profile's flexibility, the rigid idealisation does not. Had both moved, or neither, the columns would not be what the report says they are.
outcome.rigidity_caveat_ELIMINATED: anchor plate plastic strain 0%, max deformation 0.3 mm. The plate is elastic and essentially rigid, so PROFIS's Sect. 2.7 'may not behave rigid' warning no longer applies to this run.

candidate_defect_9.title: 9a: bearing resultant sits too far out (OPEN). 9b: uplift branch failed moment equilibrium (FIXED).
candidate_defect_9.found_by: PROFIS Cases C, D and E, 2026-08-30
candidate_defect_9.status: 9b fixed. 9a open — confirmed, sized, no replacement model. All three cases now err in the SAME direction.

what_is_established.large_e_branch_is_unconservative: two independent compression cases, same direction, monotone in Pu: C (Pu 150, Mu 120) -21.3%; E (Pu 500, Mu 150) -38.9%.
what_is_established.uplift_branch_fails_moment_equilibrium: FIXED 2026-08-30. T = |Pu| + Mu/(2f) implied sum(M) = Mu + Pu*f. Replaced by the signed DG 1 quadratic, unifying the branches. Case D moved from +23.7% to -6.0%.
what_is_established.compression_resultant_sits_too_far_out: PROFIS's rigid lever arm tracks its own CBFEM closely and MOVES with the load — 169.5 mm under uplift 150, 145.4 under compression 150, 131.1 under compression 500, i.e. inward as compression grows. The module's DG 1 block sits 35-50 mm further out in every case (198.8 / n.a. / 180.2).
what_is_established.magnitude_now_trustworthy: the HEB 300 control returned 276.0 against the yielded IPE 300 run's 275.997. The equivalent-rigid extraction does not see the profile, so the recorded deltas stand at full size: C -21.3%, D +23.7%, E -38.9%.

what_is_NOT_established.any_replacement_model: the flange lever arm fitted C and D within 4% and missed E by -12%. A plate-edge block with a fixed effective width needs B_eff = 173 / 85 / 249 mm across the three cases — also not constant. Neither survives three points. Do not adopt either. A one-parameter elastic rigid-plate model on a Winkler bed was also tried and did not fit any of the three. Three candidate models, none survived. Stop reverse-engineering PROFIS.

next_step.priority: STOP running PROFIS cases. The comparison has given all it can: the disagreement is real, confirmed, and sized. What is missing is not another PROFIS point but a THIRD source.
next_step.why: every measurement so far is module-vs-PROFIS. That establishes they differ; it cannot say which is wrong. The gap GROWING with axial load (-21.3% at Pu 150, -38.9% at Pu 500) is the kind of signature a subtle misapplication produces, so the module has not been cleared of one.
next_step.run: work AISC DG 1 2nd ed.'s own large-moment design example through the module by hand. No GUI needed — just the Design Guide. If the module reproduces DG 1's worked example, then DG 1 and PROFIS genuinely differ and this is a method choice. If it does not, there is a bug in the module and the method debate was premature.
next_step.bonus: the same DG 1 worked example also exercises the bearing, thickness and lambda relations, so one source can close baseplate.bearing, baseplate.thickness and baseplate.lambda as well — three of the four open base plate flags.

candidate_defect_9.why_not_fixed_here: the large-e branch implements AISC DG 1 Sect. 3.4 correctly and no validated replacement has survived testing. The uplift branch is a separate matter — its moment-equilibrium failure is provable without PROFIS and should be fixed regardless, but the fix depends on which bearing model the project adopts, so it waits on the same decision.
candidate_defect_9.decision_deferred_until: the DG 1 worked example. The uplift branch's moment-equilibrium failure is independent of all this and can be fixed now.

flags_this_can_close.baseplate.eccentricity: NOT closed. Three runs, three disagreements. The runs did their job.

flags_this_cannot_close.baseplate.bearing: AISC J8, computed library-side in pyaisc360. PROFIS does not expose a comparable number.
flags_this_cannot_close.baseplate.thickness: DG 1 cantilever method. PROFIS uses CBFEM — not comparable. Needs an AISC base-plate calculator or a hand check.
